fichas.title: Sun protection for windows
fichas.summary: Illustrations compare internal and external blinds, impact-pane protection, awnings, and partly angled Markisolette blinds. Internal blinds allow heat to build up behind the window and provide glare protection only. Awnings stop sunshine and warmth; spacing them from the wall prevents heat build-up.

fichas.title: Window requirements and design
fichas.summary: Windows provide natural light, air supply and extraction, and views, while contributing to façade appearance and interior light direction. Their location, proportions, opening type, shading, ventilation performance, safety, and maintenance require consideration. Escape-route windows require a clear opening of at least 0.9 × 1.2 m and a sill no higher than 1.2 m above floor level. In the Netherlands, window sizes are regulated in relation to the angle of incidence of light.
uses: Serve as an escape route where required
Control solar gain and light direction

fichas.title: Window sizes for residential and workrooms
fichas.summary: Window sizing guidance covers minimum structural apertures in occupied rooms, glazing-bar effects on remaining glass area, and workplace criteria. Residential apertures are specified as alternatives of 1/8 or 1/10 of room plan area. Workroom guidance gives minimum visual-connection width relative to wall width, sill-height guidance, and minimum glazing area for rooms higher than 3.5 m. For rooms comparable in size to residential rooms, the stated minimum glass-area height is 1.3 m.
uses: Provide daylight and visual connection to the outside
Account for glazing bars when replacing windows
